- When sentiment is negative (especially recent -1.00), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to avoid undershoot.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +3–5% above prior high.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive but price is trending down, model underestimates mean reversion; add 1–3% upward bias to mid-term forecast.
- When history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model often fails to recognize continuation; extend downward bias by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently >10% above true outcome over 30d, reduce long-term forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion tendency.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., 2+ swings), model overfits short-term noise; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ true values before extrapolation.
